findings.explanation: The inspected root tree contains manuscript, analysis, results and archived environment, and places the three versioned components beneath that root. This is a structural pass; it does not establish that every recursive URL or payload is retrievable.

The root inputs have public Git URLs and confirmed Gitlink identities. Following root -> data/raw_eyegaze -> src/lab-eyetracking reveals an author-host path, supporting partial under the stated inclusion of linked components. The assessment correctly distinguishes that acquisition ancestor from the files selected by the paper rerun; the defect must not be presented as an observed failure of the current analysis.

The root recipe declares scientific packages and PDF tools and installs the pinned classifier. The labels component also pins its own classifier, whose setup.py declares its scientific requirements. These are acceptable inclusion mechanisms under the native equivalent-evidence rule, independently of exact version pinning.

Read-only tree inspection confirms Git blobs for source, configuration, manuscript and numerical macros, plus explicit Gitlinks. Omitted payloads in the frozen capture are not working-tree deletions by the project.

The image layers are large, represented by tracked symlinks and MD5E annex identities in the supplied inventory. The raw-data documentation explicitly separates Git metadata from git-annex content. This supports the storage mechanism without proving current availability or recomputing payload hashes.

Partial is supported: the 2023 record connects its actual action, inputs, image and outputs, whereas the label-generation record names no exact host environment. There is an additional local gap: quality_stats() produces the manuscript velocity histogram, is not dispatched by the recorded command, and its original figure-addition commit describes a manual computation without an exact environment. Merely listing img as an output does not prove every contained figure was regenerated.
findings.suggested_correction: Retain partial and add the velocity-histogram provenance gap; qualify claims that the 2023 run covers every figure.

findings.explanation: The instructions exist, but their claim that the documented rerun recomputes every numerical value and all figure SVGs conflicts with the mechanism. quality_stats() writes img/velhist.svg and computes the displayed loss summaries, but the main dispatch never calls it. The clean targets preserve SVG sources, and main.tex includes velhist.pdf. The native documentation-versus-mechanism rule therefore precludes an unqualified met; labeling the older instructions does not disclose this current-route omission.
findings.suggested_correction: Change to partial and identify the omitted quality_stats/velhist regeneration step. Distinguish regenerated results from previously computed figure sources used for manuscript rendering.

findings.explanation: The tag resolves to the cited execution, so the starting point is real. Nevertheless it does not perform all computation promised by that starting point: the script dispatch omits quality_stats(), which creates the velocity-distribution figure included in the manuscript. Under the native route-conflict rule, this is partial rather than met, even though the command is clear and completed historically.
findings.suggested_correction: Retain credit for the concrete tagged entry point, but mark partial for the unmentioned figure-regeneration omission.

findings.explanation: The inspected current analysis constructs project-relative input and output paths. Both delivered Condor wrappers contain a fixed author working directory and Python executable. Partial accurately describes the broader linked-code scope, provided those legacy bindings are not claimed to be invoked by the current paper rerun.

The partial rationale conflates dependency inclusion with exact environment identity. The discoverable labels -> code/remodnav component has a tracked setup.py listing numpy, scipy, statsmodels and matplotlib, and its README describes Python installation. Those declarations cover the cited scientific imports even though compute_all.sh uses PYTHONPATH and does not install them itself. The native rule requires naming a genuinely omitted dependency after inspecting local/package declarations; missing locks or a run-specific environment do not establish this item.
findings.suggested_correction: Credit the linked package declaration. If retaining partial, identify a concrete undeclared requirement on the in-scope route and explain why existing declarations do not cover it. Keep the missing exact label-run environment finding under must/006 rather than using it alone here.

findings.explanation: The root documents operating systems and Docker format/version compatibility, but the adapter explicitly assumes Docker on PATH and runnable by a non-root user. The root does not spell out that permission requirement, and the legacy wrappers add inherited environment and host bindings. Partial is supported by concrete assumptions, not a quiet probe.

The documented current route lists DataLad, its container extension and Docker, while the recipe lists the internal scientific and PDF requirements. The manuscript Operation section and linked package declaration also enumerate classifier requirements. This supports the stated current-route reading; it does not cure the undeclared host assumptions separately identified under must/011.

The Git tree contains the recipe, registered invocation and image manifests alongside source and results. This criterion is about tracking environment specifications, which is directly observable despite absent image payloads.

The recorded build/save command is executable update machinery, and the later successful image conversion is an actual tracked update with image inputs and outputs. This exceeds a mere initial declaration. The frozen history confirms the conversion even though some historical blobs needed by diff display are omitted. The paired duplicate flag is present.

The current manifest names a content-derived configuration and layer identities. Historical tree inspection at the results commit shows the same f881bd4 configuration identity in the original archive layout. The inspected adapter hashes configuration bytes and runs the resulting sha256 image ID, so the internal latest RepoTag does not create a floating registry dependency. Payload bytes remain unverified.

The index and annex web log establish recorded identities and a content location, not successful retrieval by an independent recipient. Not-checked follows the native stricter access rule and this no-network boundary. An absent captured layer is not a failed download.

Acquisition and container invocation are explained accurately, but the native method explicitly maps documented-route/mechanism conflicts to this item too. The advertised complete reproduction route omits quality_stats(), while the manuscript consumes its previously computed velocity histogram. The assessment only considers the truthfully labeled old-versus-new routes and misses this separate mismatch within the current route.
findings.suggested_correction: Under the assigned native rule, use partial while preserving credit for environment acquisition instructions. State the additional computation needed or narrow the documentation claim to the outputs actually regenerated.

findings.explanation: Root and recursive component identities are consistently Git-based, with git-annex for selected large content. Different repositories and two classifier revisions do not constitute competing version-control systems.

Partial is a defensible description of a configured classifier CI route plus a completed paper analysis, with no established repeated testing of the full documented paper route. The uncalled quality_stats() is additional evidence that the instructions overstate the exercised computation. The CI file alone should remain evidence of a testing design, not an observed successful CI run.

Raw gaze and derived event labels are separate pinned datasets. The classifier has its own component, while paper analysis, figure outputs and environment files occupy separate directories. This satisfies practical separation without requiring every directory to be a separate repository.

The declared inputs are described as public, raw gaze explicitly advertises unrestricted access, and the classifier is openly licensed. No restricted component is established in the reproduction route. The unresolved local acquisition link does not by itself prove access restrictions, so the empty-subject N/A is justified within the inspected boundary.

The exit-0 historical record invokes the Docker adapter, whose inspected implementation creates a new container, and runs clean results_def.tex. This is completed execution evidence, not merely a script definition, so it satisfies the assigned rule. Its scope is the implemented analysis target: it does not prove that quality_stats(), every figure-generation step, or the full manuscript were tested in that run.
findings.suggested_correction: Keep met for the observed analysis target, but qualify the phrase full results to avoid implying coverage of all promised manuscript computations.

findings.explanation: The current paper route starts a new docker run --rm instance for each invocation. Its temporary HOME is under the mounted project directory and removed on successful completion; persistent project outputs do not make the container itself long-lived. The assessment appropriately phrases this finding about current container invocations, rather than proving historical label generation was disposable.

The historical build, analysis run and later image load/conversion demonstrate distinct maintenance events. They do not establish regular testing that the exact result environment can be reconstituted. Not-checked avoids turning lack of a schedule or retained recurring receipts into proof that no such testing occurred.

The tree and build record show the image archived as tracked configuration plus annex layers within the research object. This is more than a mutable external image reference. The assessment explicitly separates that archival structure from current retrieval, which remains unchecked.

This duplicates must/014 and is answered consistently, including the upstream-duplicate flag. A recorded update procedure and the completed image-format update support the verdict; the duplicate should not be interpreted as an independently observed second maintenance practice.

The independently maintained data and classifier components are explicitly linked and pinned. The recursive acquisition component with an author-local URL is a specific exception, so partial is defensible for this broad component boundary. Package dependencies have not been incorrectly counted as missing project modules.

The README and manuscript explain versioned code/data and reproducibility, and module maps show locations, but the labels README describes an older Condor procedure rather than its delivered compute_all.sh route. Partial appropriately recognizes documentation while identifying a concrete gap in explaining how the nested pieces fit together.

The cited evidence does not show that modular boundaries prevent independent updates. Separate pinned classifier revisions allow the paper and label dataset to evolve independently; fixed relative data paths and event schemas are ordinary interfaces. Neither a missing compatibility contract nor legacy host assumptions alone demonstrates a boundary violation. The native partial category requires a specific violation or a property holding only in identified components.
findings.suggested_correction: Do not use version differences or untested compatibility as a demonstrated modularity defect. Credit the independently pinned boundaries; if retaining partial, identify a concrete cross-boundary update dependency or break. State any untested compatibility guarantee as a limitation.

findings.explanation: The module Gitlinks, explicit selected data inputs and image registration form a concrete composition mechanism. This remains true even though an ancestral acquisition URL is not portable and one figure-generation function is omitted from the default dispatch.

The acquisition commands and recursive path-to-repository maps provide usable navigation into the linked object. This asks for documentation or tooling, so the structural tooling supports met despite the more limited explanatory documentation identified under may/002.

limitations: Inspection-only review of the frozen manifest with verified SHA256 e3c6253bced7d959cd59873c3d49d166bf5793906bcdf65e49e265076d215499. No network calls, payload acquisition, scientific execution, container build or rerun occurred.

Annex payloads, container layers and omitted figure/source blobs were unavailable by design. No present-day recipient retrieval, scientific correctness, bitwise reproduction or visual comparison is established. Missing payloads are capture limitations, not observed retrieval failures.

All Git reads used GIT_NO_LAZY_FETCH=1. Some historical show/diff requests encountered omitted promised blobs; their frozen history records and available trees were used without fetching. Original working-tree or ignored artifacts are not captured.

The root-to-component links were inspected before following their frozen source material. The adapter was reached through the root README tool/version reference and registered invocation. Its assessment citation uses a version tag; this review cites the frozen content-addressed local evidence locator instead of asserting tag immutability.

The assigned JSON and all 31 criterion rationales were reviewed. Native pin check and response validator passed; this did not establish correctness. Available cited source hashes matched the frozen files. The original probe receipt, additional assessment report and live issue/CI contents were not consulted.

The response contains 17 MUST, 9 SHOULD and 5 MAY answers. Its status counts are internally consistent: MUST 11 met, 5 partial, 1 not-checked; SHOULD 6 met, 1 partial, 1 not-checked, 1 not-applicable; MAY 2 met, 3 partial. No aggregate score or denominator claim is included in the supplied JSON to audit further.

The broad linked-component scope exposes genuine ancestral defects, but those must be kept distinct from the prerequisites of the current numerical rerun. Agreement here is an independent evidence judgment, not human approval.
